articles.title: SJAA's School Star Party Program Needs Your Help!
articles.summary: The San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA) is seeking volunteers for its School Star Party (SSP) program, which introduces astronomy to students and families. The program's long-time leader has retired, necessitating a new team to manage and modernize the initiative. SJAA is looking to fill several distinct roles, including Program Leader, Liaison, Scout, and Astronomers, to ensure the continuation of this popular educational outreach.

articles.title: Cupertino Earth Day Report
articles.summary: The article reports on the San Jose Astronomical Association's (SJAA) participation in the 10th annual Cupertino Earth Day Festival, marking their 6th consecutive year attending. SJAA members set up solar telescopes, including a new Lunt H-alpha scope with a video camera and monitor for public viewing, and staffed a table with astronomical photo books and membership information. The event facilitated public engagement with astronomy, particularly solar viewing, and outreach about SJAA activities.

articles.title: SJAA Logo-Wear!
articles.summary: This article from Marianne Damon announces that SJAA members can now easily create their own custom logo-wear using a new webpage on the SJAA website. It provides step-by-step instructions for downloading the logo, selecting a company, designing items like shirts or bags with the SJAA logo and optional personalized text. The author also shares her positive experience with the process and encourages members to proudly display the club's logo at events to enhance visibility.

articles.title: What in the World is an 'Exoplanet?'
articles.summary: Exoplanets are worlds orbiting stars beyond our Sun, ranging from gas giants to rocky planets, varying widely in temperature, orbital period, and number of suns. Humans have only recently confirmed their existence, with the first definitive discovery in 1995 (51 Pegasi b), though some hints emerged earlier. The number of confirmed exoplanets is rapidly increasing due to advanced telescopes, and scientists hope to detect signs of life on these distant worlds in the future.

articles.title: Hubble Uncovers the Farthest Star Ever Seen
articles.summary: NASA's Hubble Space Telescope has identified Icarus (MACS J1149+2223 Lensed Star 1), the farthest individual star ever seen, located 9 billion light-years away. Its visibility is due to gravitational lensing by a massive galaxy cluster, which tremendously amplified its faint glow. This discovery offers a new method to study individual stars in distant galaxies, providing insights into stellar evolution and dark matter.

articles.title: SJAA Member Astrophoto Gallery
articles.summary: This article showcases an astrophotography gallery by members of the San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA). It features stunning images of deep-sky objects such as M101, M51, M106, and the Leo Triplet, captured by different photographers. Each entry provides detailed information about the imaging equipment, software, and techniques used by the contributing members.

articles.title: Kid Spot
articles.summary: The 'Kid Spot' section provides engaging content for young readers interested in astronomy. It features a collection of space-themed jokes designed for entertainment, alongside a multiple-choice quiz to test basic knowledge on topics such as celestial phenomena, distant objects in our solar system, and key historical moments in space exploration.

articles.title: Hubble Finds an Einstein Ring
articles.summary: The Hubble Space Telescope has discovered an Einstein Ring, named SDSS J0146-0929, formed by a massive galaxy cluster. This cosmic phenomenon occurs when the light from a distant background galaxy is distorted and diverted by the cluster's immense gravity, making the galaxy appear in multiple places at once and forming distinctive arcs around the cluster's center.

articles.title: From the Board of Directors
articles.summary: The SJAA Board of Directors convened in March and April 2018, electing Swami Nigam as President and Emi Nikolov as Ephemeris Production editor, while actively seeking to fill vacant positions including Ephemeris Content Editor, Librarian, and a board seat. Key initiatives discussed and approved included a new loaner solar scope, a new welcome email for members, progress on a contract with the City of San Jose, and plans for a potential star party at Kelley Park, alongside research into making SJAA logo wear available.

articles.title: SJAA Library and Programs
articles.summary: The San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA) provides diverse programs and resources for its members and the community, ranging from beginner to advanced levels. These offerings include a library, telescope repair services, solar observing sessions, introductory astronomy courses (Quick STARt, Intro to the Night Sky), an equipment loaner program, and astrophotography special interest groups and workshops. Additionally, the SJAA conducts school star parties and publishes a quarterly newsletter, "Ephemeris," with contact information for various program leads.
